director.chapterArc: Tactical instruction shifts to combat chaos, then collapses into physical exhaustion and a revelation of Wyck's passive power before resolving in a stoic debrief about the gap between knowledge and action.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's analytical distance even during panic; do not let his internal fear become melodramatic. The narrator remains an older, cooler observer filtering through Toren's sensory experience. Wyck's revelation is delivered with quiet shock, not triumph. Rook's final lines are matter-of-fact, avoiding lecturing tones.

cues.delivery: Instructional calm. Rook's voice is flat and factual; the narrator treats this as a tactical briefing rather than a dramatic monologue.
cues.from: "Stilts, is what I call them. They stand about as high as me, and about nine-tenths of it is leg. Two legs, jointed backwards, longer than they've any business being, and a body slung between them no bigger than a dog, and a head you won't be able to find and won't need to. Colour of wet ash, same as the hounds, same as everything.
cues.through: "Stand where the trees are. Never stand at the end of a row. If you find yourself looking down a long clear stretch of anything, you are already in the wrong place, and you should move before you finish the thought."
cues.reason: Establishes the 'lines' doctrine without emotional padding.

cues.delivery: Urgent internal monologue. Toren's spine goes cold; the narration accelerates slightly to match his physical reaction and rapid speech.
cues.from: Toren's whole spine went cold, and his mouth was already moving.
cues.through: Toren caught that part in pieces, out of order, and had to sort them afterward. Rook's weight had already gone onto the forward foot before the hound cleared the hedge. The light came out along the outside of his right forearm and took its edge on the way, from the wrist outward, the way a crack takes across ice. Then the arm went across at hip height. Once. Level. Without hurry.
cues.reason: Captures the immediate spike of adrenaline before combat begins.

cues.delivery: Clinical description. The violence is described physically ('crack takes across ice') without romanticizing the impact.
cues.from: The hound's front leg came off at the shoulder. It ran three more steps on what it had already spent, turned over, slid, and went to ash in the dock leaves.
cues.through: The hound's front leg came off at the shoulder. It ran three more steps on what it had already spent, turned over, slid, and went to ash in the dock leaves.
cues.reason: Maintains narrator distance during combat action.

cues.delivery: Dry relief. Milo's laughter is high-pitched and nervous; Toren's internal state is 'ringing' ears.
cues.from: Milo was laughing in the high way he had when he had been frightened. "He called it. Tor called it before it moved."
cues.through: He did not say anything else. Toren walked the next two miles with his ears ringing and his chest about four inches further out than it had started the morning, and every step of those two miles laid down a little more of the thing that was going to cost them at four o'clock.
cues.reason: Contrasts the tension of combat with post-battle exhaustion.

cues.delivery: Observational precision. Toren's eye records the Stilt as a visual anomaly; the rhythm is steady and rhythmic.
cues.from: The first one Toren saw stood three rows down and eighty feet along, between two trees, so still and so exactly the colour of the grey trunks that he looked straight through it twice. What gave it away in the end had nothing to do with shape. Every trunk in that orchard carried the same yellow lichen up its north side. The thing standing between them carried none.
cues.through: Then the row discipline worked, and it worked so well that it was almost boring.
cues.reason: Focuses on sensory details of the enemy rather than emotional reaction.

cues.delivery: Mechanical explanation. Wyck's kill is described as a physical mechanism ('stepladder coming apart'), not a heroic feat.
cues.from: Toren got a proper look at one in that state, ten feet off, while it worked out how to come at them through four trunks that had grown together at the base. The foot was the whole answer to the thing. It had no toes and no pad: one hard black point, like the ferrule on the end of a stick, set into the turf under all that weight. To move the leg at all it had to draw the point up out of the ground. The point came up with a plug of soil on it. It left a clean round divot behind, and a little ridge of pushed turf standing in front of the divot, where it had loaded. Then it set the point down again somewhere else, and that was the choosing. That was the entire mechanism. A point can drive. A point cannot steer.
cues.through: He let it come inside the trunks and inside the length of the bar. The knee of its left leg jointed backwards, the way they all did; he did not swing against the bend, he swung with it, two hands, low and flat, the whole weight of his shoulders going through the middle of the bar into the joint. The joint went the way it already wanted to go, and then further than it wanted to go. The leg folded. The creature came apart downward, all its height arriving on the ground at once, like a stepladder coming apart.

cues.delivery: Self-critical panic. Toren's internal monologue is frantic; the narration reflects his realization of error and immediate danger.
cues.from: He went to it instead of letting it come. That was the mistake, and he knew it while he did it. The first thrust went in under the slung body and came out with nothing on it. The second skidded off the top of the haunch; he had his weight forward on the front foot and could not turn with the thing when the thing turned. It came round on its planted point. That put him outside the trunk line, in the open, with the whole clear length of the fourth row standing at his back.
cues.through: By the time Toren had the rest of the sentence out, nobody stood in the row behind him.
cues.reason: Highlights Toren's tactical failure under pressure.

cues.delivery: Sudden urgency. Dessa's voice cuts through; the narration accelerates to match the breach of the ditch.
cues.from: She said it in a completely different voice from the one she had been using, and it went across the orchard like a thrown stone.
cues.through: "Down!" Rook shouted, from somewhere up the slope. "Everyone west — press-house — now, go, go—"
cues.reason: Signals the shift from controlled drill to chaotic survival.

cues.delivery: Stunned observation. Rook's movement is described as 'ordinary' and unhurried; the narrator notes the lack of noise.
cues.from: Toren had not known that was possible. He could never get it back in order afterward, only in pieces, and the pieces would not add up to enough time. The thing came out of the mouth of the ditch on a line for the steps. Rook went to meet it, and the going was the part that would not make sense, because Rook did not run. He took two ordinary steps up onto the coping stone at the ditch lip — ordinary, unhurried, a man stepping up onto a kerb. The struts fired under him, one flat report. He came up off the stone already turned and already at the height the thing's body rode at, with no part of the movement spent getting there.
cues.through: Toren saw the point of its right foot set into the clay. He saw the little ridge of pushed turf standing up in front of it, where it had loaded. He looked straight at it.
cues.reason: Emphasizes the unnatural efficiency of combat.

cues.delivery: Catastrophic realization. Toren's panic peaks; the Ember activation is described as a physical release ('world went very simple'), not magical wonder.
cues.from: Toren's whole spine went cold. The cold came with a name already on it. The name was a gift. It was the wrong gift, and it was his.
cues.through: He felt it go. It ran out of his fist in one clean movement — thinner, half again as long, the edge arriving before the length had finished arriving — and it was not ugly at all. The light did not stop at his knuckles this time. It went back up over his wrist and took the whole of his forearm, and the world went very simple.
cues.reason: Captures the moment of total exhaustion and power expenditure.

cues.delivery: Physical collapse. Toren is incapacitated; Wyck's intervention is described with clinical precision ('water comes off a gatepost').
cues.from: There was nothing at all. The bottom came out of him the way the bottom comes out of a wet sack.
cues.through: He should have. Nine stone of boy, and a thing that had crossed forty feet in no time at all, and it came off him the way water comes off a gatepost. Wyck's boots stood exactly where Wyck's boots had been standing. The clay under them did not even give.
cues.reason: Maintains narrator distance during the climax of physical action.

cues.delivery: Revelatory calm. Rook's explanation is delivered with flat authority; Wyck's voice 'comes apart' slightly.
cues.from: "Two of them hit you at full run and you're standing where you were standing."
cues.through: "They'll never put you in a book for it. You can't show it to anybody. You can only be it, and you have been being it since before I met you, and it's the least impressive and most useful thing on this hillside."
cues.reason: Delivers the thematic core of passive Ember without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Exhausted realism. Toren's physical state is described as humiliating; Rook's dialogue is terse and factual.
cues.from: Toren could not stand until nearly dark.
cues.reason: Grounds the emotional weight in physical reality.

cues.delivery: Stoic debrief. Rook's voice is flat and measured; the final line lands with quiet authority.
cues.from: The debrief was that night, in the lee of the windbreak, with the lamp on the cart shaft and all five of them where he could see them.
cues.through: "Both of them are trainable," said Rook. "That's all. Go to sleep."
cues.reason: Concludes the scene without emotional overreach.

pauses.after: "So don't watch them. Watch the lines."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on tactical doctrine; allows listener to process 'Watch the lines'.

pauses.after: Toren had gone to sleep with his hand on a warm stone thinking that this was the easiest thing anyone had ever asked him to remember.
pauses.reason: Transition from instruction to action; breath for Toren's confidence.

pauses.after: "Right," he said. "One right, in the hedge, it's gone still, it's choosing — it's going to come and it's coming right, everybody right—"
pauses.reason: Urgent command sequence ends; pause before the hound appears.
Scene reset after combat action; shift to post-battle observation.

pauses.after: There were four of them in the orchard, which was what Rook had said there would be.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on positioning; pause before the first Stilt appears.

pauses.after: "Ditch — the ditch, the ditch, there's things in the ditch — three — four, four in the ditch and they're coming up it, they're coming west —"
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The ditch breach changes everything. Needs time for realization of danger.

pauses.after: "Down!" Rook shouted, from somewhere up the slope. "Everyone west — press-house — now, go, go—"
pauses.reason: Command to retreat; pause before the chaotic run begins.
Scene turn: The Stilt stops. A moment of stillness before Toren's error.

pauses.after: He put it through the first Stilt lengthwise, in under the body and out through the far shoulder of it, and did not slow down for the resistance, because there was no resistance. The second one came off the steps at him with its point already set. He took both legs off it on the backswing, at the same height, one pass, and neither of them touched the ground before he had turned for a third.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Ember activation and immediate collapse. Needs time for the physical sensation to register.

pauses.after: He held the gap for about eleven seconds.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on Wyck's feat; pause before Rook arrives.
Speaker reset: Shift from physical care to the revelation of Ember status.
Pause for Wyck's denial; allows his voice 'to come apart' naturally.
Completed thought on Toren's humiliation; pause before Rook's diagnosis.
Speaker reset: Shift from physical recovery to the debrief setup.

pauses.after: "Because you turned the line for two seconds," he said, "instead of four.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on Toren's error; pause before Rook's counter-argument.
